name: Water cutting / dehydration pre-photo

card.summary: Restricting fluids to look drier or sharper for a photo; dehydration has well-documented health risks.
card.note: Dehydration impairs cognition and can be dangerous at larger losses.

quick.overview:
Water cutting means deliberately limiting fluids, sometimes alongside other measures, shortly before a photo, show or weigh-in so the body looks drier and more defined. It originates in physique sport and is sometimes discussed in appearance communities.

No studies of its effect on appearance were found, while the health effects of dehydration are well documented.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say less water under the skin and in tissues gives a tighter, more defined look. Body water loss reduces blood volume and tissue hydration.
quick.risks: Medical sources report that losing 1 to 2 percent of body water can impair thinking, 5 to 8 percent can cause fatigue and dizziness, and losses above 10 percent can cause serious decline. Reference material links intentional dehydration to higher death rates among bodybuilders.

lead: Water cutting, or pre-photo dehydration, is the practice of intentionally limiting fluid intake in the hours or days before a photograph, contest or weigh-in in order to look drier or more defined. It is described as part of the final stage of bodybuilding contest preparation, which combines carbohydrate loading with dehydration [1].

Medical references describe dehydration as causing thirst, headache, fatigue and reduced urination, with cognitive impairment from losses of 1 to 2 percent of body water and life-threatening effects at much larger losses [2]. Reference material lists intentional dehydration among practices linked to higher mortality among bodybuilders [1]. No studies of its appearance effects were found.

paras: Competitors cut fat for roughly 12 to 14 weeks and, in the last stage, combine carbohydrate loading with dehydration to improve definition and vascularity [1]. Some people outside competition adopt short fluid restriction before photos. Specific protocols are not described here.

Symptoms include thirst, headache, nausea, less frequent urination, dry mucous membranes and dizziness on standing. Losses of about 3 to 4 percent of body water are usually tolerated, 5 to 8 percent can cause fatigue and dizziness, more than 10 percent brings serious physical and mental decline, and 15 to 25 percent can be fatal. Complications include hypernatremia, kidney problems, heatstroke, seizures and hypovolemic shock [2].
No studies found on water cutting for photographic appearance. General medical literature on dehydration is summarised above [2].

lore.intro: Water cutting is discussed in physique and lean-look threads as a last-minute tactic.

claims.claim: Dehydrating makes you look sharper in photos.
claims.believers: Proponents say the skin looks tighter and muscles more visible.
claims.experts: Reference material lists dehydration as part of contest prep [1]; no study measured appearance outcomes.

claims.claim: A short water cut has no meaningful downside.
claims.believers: Some users call it harmless if brief.
claims.experts: Even mild dehydration can impair cognition, and severe loss can be fatal [2]; intentional dehydration is linked to higher death rates in bodybuilders [1].
